verdicts.reason: A squeezes the mint panel into a narrow off-centre column with large areas of bare wood on the right. The headline is jammed against the top edge, and both side blurbs are stacked below it at a tiny, illegible size, so the original three-column structure and its balance are lost. B keeps the three-column banner with a readable headline and side copy that read left to right, but 'WORLD!' wraps onto a line of its own and the panel has very little space above and below the text.
